name: Nganasan
notes: Nganasan (ня’ануасана баа), Samoyedic branch, Taymyr Peninsula, Russia. INPUT CONTRACT: Nganasan Cyrillic orthography (1990s standardisation, Wagner-Nagy 2018), NFC. Two letters outside the Russian alphabet carry distinctive phonemes with no plain-letter decomposition: ⟨з̌⟩ /ð/ (a voiced interdental fricative, NorthEuraLex хиаз̌әә -> x i ɐ ð əː) and the apostrophe ⟨ˮ⟩ marking a glottal stop /ʔ/ (NorthEuraLex хебтыˮ -> x e b t ɨ ʔ). ⟨ә⟩ and ⟨ы⟩ are two distinct reduced/high-central vowels, /ə/ and /ɨ/ (Wagner-Nagy 2018, Sec. 2.1). The dental stops ⟨д⟩ and ⟨т⟩ have palatalised correlates realised as the palatal stops /ɟ/ and /c/ (Wagner-Nagy 2018, Sec. 2.2) — ⟨дь⟩ is entered directly as /ɟ/ and ⟨ч⟩ (the palatal affricate letter, used for the /c/ reflex) as /c/; before the iotated vowels ⟨е и ю я⟩ and the soft sign ⟨ь⟩, ⟨с⟩ and ⟨д⟩ additionally palatalise to /sʲ/ and /dʲ/ (directly evidenced by NorthEuraLex сеймы -> sʲ e j m ɨ and сиәде -> sʲ i ə dʲ e), so those sequences are entered as multigraph keys the maximal-munch matcher prefers over the bare consonant. Word stress in Nganasan is governed by a syllable-weight algorithm rather than a fixed position and is not simply orthography-predictable (Wagner-Nagy 2018, Sec. 2.4); documented here as an ENGINE-LIMIT stress exemption and not modelled. ITERATION FIX (error-analysis pass against NorthEuraLex): ⟨а⟩ corrected to the reduced central /ɐ/ (not /a/, NorthEuraLex ня -> ɲɐ, дяті -> dʲɐti); a complete ⟨н⟩-palatalisation series added (⟨не ни ню ня⟩ -> /ɲe ɲi ɲu ɲɐ/, on the same evidence as the already-declared ⟨нь⟩ -> /ɲ/, e.g. NorthEuraLex негыр -> ɲegɨr); and ⟨дя⟩/⟨дю⟩ added to the existing ⟨де⟩/⟨ди⟩/⟨дь⟩ palatalisation set (NorthEuraLex дяӈ -> dʲɐŋ). Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog.
